title: The mat board warps
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
source: lore/drift_wood/_THE_COMPLETE_RUN.md (1999–2000 · deepening xix · the daily filled)
logline: Tuesday. The heat gets into the shop. Mat board warps in the rack. The owner turns the boards every hour like bread. Wood learns to feel a warp with a thumb. A sheet of glass on the felt, hot to the touch. Nothing cuts right. She closes at two.

panels.composition: The shop in heat. The OWNER turning sheets of mat board in the rack. WOOD with a thumb on a board's edge, feeling.

image.prompt: a woman in reading glasses turning sheets of mat board in a rack while a young man tests a board's edge with his thumb in a hot shop, black and white, no words

panels.composition: A board, warped: a curve where a flat should be. The thumb on it.

image.prompt: close on a sheet of mat board with a slight curve along its edge under a thumb, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The glass on the felt. The owner's palm flat on it. Hot.

image.prompt: close on a woman's palm pressed flat to a pane of glass on a felt table, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The owner turning the door's card to CLOSED at two. Wood and the boards. Nothing cut today. The tally on the wall: none added. First day of none.

image.prompt: a woman turning a shop door's sign to closed in afternoon heat while a young man stands by a rack of boards, black and white, no words

art.line: brush-pen, committed; black and white; xerox

notes: First day with no cuts. The boards turned like bread.
